title: Finite root site comparison with scalar and scheme coherence
statement:
Let $m\geq1$, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $mA=0$, and let $T$ be a scheme on which $m$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme]. On the small etale and pro-etale sites use their comparison $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{et}}$ for the etale sheaf of units $z$ with $z^m=1$ [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] and $\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}$ for the same root functor on weakly etale tests [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. Put $E_{m,T}=\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/m)_{T_{\mathrm{et}}}}A_{T_{\mathrm{et}}}$ and $D_{m,T}=\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/m)_{T_{\mathrm{proet}}}}A_{T_{\mathrm{proet}}}$.

There are canonical $(\mathbf Z/m)$-linear and $A$-linear isomorphisms
$$c_{m,T}:\nu_T^{-1}\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{pro}},\qquad \sigma_{m,T}:\nu_T^*E_{m,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{m,T}.$$
For every weakly etale $f:W\to T$, identify $(\nu_T^{-1}\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{et}})(W)$ with $\Gamma(W_{\mathrm{et}},f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{et}})$ and then with $\{z\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)^\times:z^m=1\}$. Under this identification $c_{m,T}$ sends a root to that same unit. The map $\sigma_{m,T}$ is the canonical balanced-tensor comparison followed by $c_{m,T}\otimes1$, with constant scalars unchanged. Equivalently, for an etale $U\to T$, a pro-etale test $W\to T$, and a $T$-map $f:W\to U$, the comparison-adjunction unit sends a local tensor $z\otimes a$ on $U$ to a section whose restriction to $W$ is carried by $\sigma_{m,T}$ to $f^\sharp(z)\otimes a$.

For every $v:T'\to T$, let $e^v_m:v_{\mathrm{et}}^*E_{m,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{m,T'}$ be the etale root-tensor pullback along the etale inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and let $d^v_m:v_{\mathrm{proet}}^*D_{m,T}\to D_{m,T'}$ be induced by the canonical pro-etale root map adjoint to pullback of units [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Under the canonical comparison square [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] $\kappa_v:v_{\mathrm{proet}}^*\nu_T^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\nu_{T'}^*v_{\mathrm{et}}^*$ one has
$$d^v_m\,v_{\mathrm{proet}}^*\sigma_{m,T}=\sigma_{m,T'}\,\nu_{T'}^*(e^v_m)\,\kappa_v.$$
In particular $d^v_m$ is invertible. These equations, and the corresponding root-only equations for $c_{m,T}$, respect identities and composites. For $m\mid m'$ with $m'$ invertible on $T$, the root power map $z\mapsto z^{m'/m}$ commutes with $c_{m,T}$ and $\sigma_{m,T}$ (using the same $A$, killed by $m$), with the evident reductions of constant scalar rings. No affine, Noetherian or finite-type hypothesis on $T$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-comparison-pullback-sections] to the underlying set sheaf of $\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{et}}$. At each weakly etale $f:W\to T$ it identifies its comparison inverse image with $\Gamma(W_{\mathrm{et}},f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{et}})$. Since $m$ is invertible on $T$, it is invertible on $W$. The root pullback isomorphism of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] identifies the latter group with $\mu_{m,W}^{\mathrm{et}}(W)$, exactly the roots in $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)^\times$. Its compatibility with composition identifies restriction along $g:W'\to W$ with $g^\sharp$ on those roots. These bijections therefore assemble to $c_{m,T}$ with target [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. Multiplication of roots and integer powers are preserved by the root pullback maps; thus this is an abelian-sheaf isomorphism. Both sheaves are killed by $m$, so [lem-pur-torsion-sheaf-constant-module] makes it $(\mathbf Z/m)$-linear. This establishes the stated sectionwise identification on every test, without an affineness restriction.

source.place: Tag 0GLZ, lemma-describe-pullback-from-etale, applied to the finite etale root sheaf

proof.text: For etale $U/T$, the unit clause of [lem-cbc-comparison-pullback-sections] identifies the comparison unit on a root $z$ with that same section over $U$. Restricting along any $T$-map $f:W\to U$, the restriction calculation of step 1 sends it to $f^\sharp(z)$. For $m\mid m'$ put $q=m'/m$. Naturality of that section comparison in the coefficient sheaf, and the power transition in [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], identify the two composites with $z\mapsto z^q$ on every weakly etale test. In particular $f^\sharp(z^q)=f^\sharp(z)^q$. This proves the unit normalization and the root-only power square.

source.place: Tag 0GLZ, naturality of the section formula and its restriction to etale objects

proof.text: Put $B=(\mathbf Z/m)_{T_{\mathrm{et}}}$. The geometric inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] transports the ring and module operations by finite products, giving the algebraic inverse-image presentation of [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] to $M=\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{et}}$ and $N=A_{T_{\mathrm{et}}}$ as $B$-modules. By [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact](1), with coefficient rings $\mathbf Z/m$ and $A$, the pulled-back constant rings identify with the corresponding pro-etale constant rings and the fixed-coefficient module pullback is the underlying inverse image. These identifications preserve constant sections: their adjuncts are the constant-section maps defining the comparison. Hence the tensor comparison followed by $c_{m,T}\otimes1$ gives an $A$-linear isomorphism $\sigma_{m,T}$. The $A$-action is multiplication on the second tensor factor; naturality of the tensor comparison in that multiplication makes this map $A$-linear. Its generalized pure-tensor formula and step 2 give $z\otimes a\mapsto f^\sharp(z)\otimes a$ on the unit followed by restriction. This is the asserted balanced-tensor map; no flatness assumption on $A$ over $\mathbf Z/m$ was used.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; constant-ring identifications and the root comparison
Tag 0GLZ together with canonical comparison of the two composite inverse images; adjunction-unit calculation

proof.text: For tensor coefficients the pro-etale constant-ring map is the constant-section isomorphism of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], applied to $A$ and $\mathbf Z/m$. Thus $d_m^v$ is induced by the root map just used and the unchanged scalars. The tensor comparisons for all the geometric inverse images have the normalized formula of [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison]; their algebraic lifts are the transported operations in the inverse-image definitions. Take composite adjuncts of the two sides of the desired equation, as in step 4. On every pure section $z\otimes a$ of $E_{m,T}$ over etale $U/T$ they both give $\mathrm{pr}_U^\sharp(z)\otimes a$: first use the formula for $\sigma$, then the root-square formula and the constant-section map. A scalar section is locally a constant section by [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], so the equality holds for arbitrary scalar sections too. The tensor universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] shows the adjuncts are equal on the sheaf tensor, hence the original arrows are equal. This proves $d_m^v v_{\mathrm{proet}}^*\sigma_{m,T}=\sigma_{m,T'}\nu_{T'}^*(e_m^v)\kappa_v$. Every factor on the right and $v_{\mathrm{proet}}^*\sigma_{m,T}$ is invertible, so $d_m^v$ is invertible. Invertibility of $m$ on $T'$ follows by pulling back its inverse.

source.place: Tag 03EL, pure-tensor normalization; equality tested after adjunction and bilinear universality

proof.text: For an identity scheme map the root formula is $z\mapsto z$; for $T''\xrightarrow{w}T'\xrightarrow{v}T$ the iterated formula is $z\mapsto\mathrm{pr}_w^\sharp(\mathrm{pr}_v^\sharp z)$, equal to pullback along the composite under the canonical fibre-product identification. The constant scalar is unchanged. Equality of the corresponding adjuncts, then [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal], proves the identity and composition laws for $c$, $d$ and the displayed $\sigma$ squares. These use exactly the identity/composition comparisons in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Finally for $m\mid m'$ the transition is $z\otimes a\mapsto z^{m'/m}\otimes a$. It is balanced over $\mathbf Z/m'$ into the tensor over $\mathbf Z/m$ because powers commute with integer multiplication and the action on $A$ factors through $\mathbf Z/m$. The step-2 root square and the step-3 tensor formula give this same value on both sides of the $\sigma$ power square; bilinear universality again proves equality. The same calculation commutes with scheme pullback since pullback of units commutes with powers. This proves every coherence assertion, including $m=1$, the zero ring, and the empty scheme.
